assetRisk.scenario: Distribution network overpressurization or regulator control failure
assetRisk.source: ~450 district regulating stations (DRS) and city gate regulating skids across ~16-20 municipal geographical areas. Frequency of 0.008 events per station-year reflects ~1 significant pressure excursion, regulator seat lock-up failure, or relief valve venting challenge per 125 station-years, benchmarked against international distribution pipeline safety data (PHMSA 49 CFR Part 191 incident trends and NTSB accident reports). Consequence of INR 12 Cr (~$1.44M) covers emergency sectional shut-in, rapid street-by-street isolation, replacement of overpressurized domestic meters and customer service regulators, property and burner repairs, manual relighting sweeps across thousands of premises (averaging INR 15,000-25,000 per customer connection for labor-intensive relighting and safety checks across 4,000-6,000 premises), civil repair, and statutory regulatory penalties (under PNGRB T4S / ASME B31.8 / 49 CFR 192). Alpha (0.35) reflects the causal share attributable to engineering design errors, incorrect valve sizing coefficients, common-mode sense line routing, and inadequate relief capacity (as documented in NTSB pipeline accident investigations); beta (0.40) captures the agent squad's verified efficacy in automated regulator sizing (Agent 4), sense line independence auditing (Agent 5), and MAOP envelope validation (Agent 3).

rationale: P44 Gas Distribution Engineer governs the design, hydraulic simulation, overpressure protection architecture, and distribution integrity management (DIMP) across the municipal City Gas Distribution (CGD) footprint (~20,000-25,000 km of steel feeder mains and PE distribution grids across ~16-20 authorized geographical areas). Headcount of 50 seats represents ~1.04% of total enterprise headcount (4,800), comprising ~38 regional distribution network planning and extension engineers (~2 per geographical area) and ~12 central engineering specialists (hydraulic simulation, overpressure protection envelopes, and DIMP risk ranking). ASSET_CAPITAL is strictly null: distribution planning and design workflows occur offline on engineering workstations and do not sit on the critical path of flowing gas or operating pressure assets (strictly adhering to value_model.js critical-path rules, identical to P27 Pipeline Integrity and P30 Inspection). ASSET_RISK models distribution network overpressurization and regulator station control failure across 450 district regulating stations at INR 12 Cr consequence with alpha*beta held to 0.14 (yielding INR 6.05 Cr/yr in avoided expected loss). RESOURCE_RECOVERY is null because midstream distribution operates downstream of production and cannot alter subsurface recoverable reserves, and value_model.js prohibits joint integrity and recovery claims.
caveats: Asset capital is deliberately null: distribution network planning, hydraulic bottleneck screening, MAOP derating, and DIMP risk scoring occur offline and do not sit on the critical path of flowing gas or running machinery. If an operator insists on parameterizing avoided winter peak low-pressure curtailment as an asset lever, it would be formulated in volume form (e.g., 0.05% of peak unserved volume recovered), but is omitted here to prevent double-counting against live control-room dispatch (P14 Pipeline Controller) and maintain value model credibility. DRS overpressure risk consequence (INR 12 Cr) reflects a contained municipal overpressure excursion requiring customer relighting and regulator replacements; catastrophic multi-structure explosion events (e.g., Merrimack Valley class, exceeding $1B) are treated as tail-risk scenarios outside the baseline model.
